page: Amazon Web Services r8idn.12xlarge is an eighth-generation memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. Powered by Intel x86_64 processors operating at clock speeds up to 3.9 GHz, the server delivers 48 dedicated virtual CPUs across 24 physical cores with two threads per core. The instance configuration includes 384.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio designed to handle memory-intensive execution environments without resource contention.

The hardware configuration features bundled local high-speed storage in the form of a 2850 GB NVMe SSD volume, eliminating the need to rely solely on remote volumes for IO-heavy scratch operations. Network capabilities include a baseline bandwidth of 75 Gbps, facilitating rapid inter-node data exchange and dedicated connectivity to Elastic Block Store volumes. The system does not include discrete GPU accelerators, focusing purely on host CPU compute and large memory density.

By delivering a large memory footprint alongside high-throughput local NVMe storage, the server provides favorable resource density for latency-sensitive applications. Because local instance storage is ephemeral, architectures require external persistence for durable state management. The r8idn.12xlarge is suited for in-memory key-value databases, distributed caching layers, transaction-intensive relational database engines, and real-time big data processing frameworks.
description: Amazon Web Services r8idn.12xlarge is a memory-optimized instance engineered for enterprise applications requiring high memory density, substantial local I/O, and high network throughput. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, the platform features 48 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs across 24 Intel physical cores running at up to 3.9 GHz, paired with 384.0 GB of system memory to maintain an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. Storage capabilities include 2850 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD instance storage, enabling high-speed scratch space and low-latency cache layers. Baseline network bandwidth is configured at 75 Gbps, facilitating rapid inter-node communication and data synchronization across large distributed clusters. Lacking hardware accelerators such as GPUs, computational execution relies entirely on the host CPUs. The architecture is suited for high-throughput transactional databases, distributed in-memory caches, Apache Spark or Hadoop analytics nodes, and real-time data streaming workloads that benefit from expansive memory alongside fast ephemeral storage.
